extracted.intended_audience: European Commission officials preparing policy initiatives, impact assessments, evaluations/fitness checks, and managers responsible for quality control and implementation
extracted.subtask_short: preparing EU impact assessments and consultations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Commission staff on how to plan, conduct and quality-control stakeholder consultations, evaluations/fitness checks, impact assessments, implementation strategies and monitoring to produce evidence-informed, proportionate and transparent EU policy proposals and legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive evaluations and fitness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive evaluations and fitness checks involve thorough analysis of how existing legislation and spending programmes have been performing, to check that they are efficient, effective, relevant and coherent, and that EU-level intervention is actually adding value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fitness checks are comprehensive evaluations of a policy area, addressing how a set of related legislative acts contributed to policy objectives and are particularly suited to identifying regulatory overlaps, inconsistencies, synergies, digitalisation potential and cumulative impacts. Evaluations should monitor effects of implementation and application to enable meaningful future evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact assessment (general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact assessments look at the problems to be tackled, the objectives to be achieved, the trade-offs to consider, options for action and their potential impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must identify and describe the problem, establish objectives, formulate policy options and assess potential impacts, identify a preferred option where appropriate, and set out monitoring and evaluation arrangements. Use an integrated approach assessing environmental, social and economic impacts and mainstream sustainability/SDGs where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder consultation as essential element
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder consultation is an essential element of policy preparation and review: stakeholders provide contributions to support evaluations, impact assessments and preparation of initiatives and political decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan consultations with a concise strategy identifying relevant stakeholders and targeting them with a range of activities; consult as widely as possible while avoiding consultation fatigue; ensure respondents receive feedback on how contributions were used. Public consultation is an essential element of impact assessments and can be useful for many evaluations and fitness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance promotion and implementation support
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance promotion tools help Member States transpose, implement and apply EU law in a timely and correct manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools include guidance documents, expert groups, explanatory documents, training, workshops and package meetings. Use a combination of tools regularly to prevent or correct breaches and to avoid referral to the Court. Choose tools with regard to Commission competences, instrument type, national systems and burden on Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive approach (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations should cover all relevant economic, social and environmental impacts, all interested parties and every phase in the policy cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant impacts on gender equality, territorial and rural issues, geopolitical context, external implications on third countries, competitiveness and SMEs must be screened and presented transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent approach (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure consistency of proposed law with high-level and long-term policy objectives and across services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply principles like 'do no significant harm' and 'digital by default', implement European Climate Law commitments, advance digital-ready policymaking, and integrate SDGs and strategic foresight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionate approach (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The approach should be proportionate to the expected impacts and analysis should focus on areas where it matters most.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depth of analysis should reflect significance of impacts. Guidelines and toolbox should be applied in a proportionate manner using common sense; exemptions allowed in emergencies or where justified via political validation or SG exceptions mailbox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participative approach (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: All interested parties, including experts, individuals and groups affected by EU laws, should be able to contribute to policymaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure inclusive consultation strategies and provide opportunities for contributions at stages where views can still make a difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based approach (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy decisions need to be informed by the best available evidence, including scientific evidence where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence includes quantitative and qualitative data, stakeholder input, evaluation conclusions, and expert advice. Use open data sources (e.g., data.europa.eu) and operational tools in the 'better regulation' toolbox (Tool #4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare laws and regulation in a transparent way by documenting the process, making evidence available and explaining the rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish consultation documents and contributions on 'Have Your Say' portal and, where possible, on DG websites. RSB opinions are published in the Register of Commission Documents once the Commission adopts the legislative proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning from experience / 'evaluate first' principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Policymakers need to learn from experience of implementing and applying EU rules; the 'evaluate first' principle should apply whenever legislation is revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use evaluations to check performance versus earlier expectations and to determine whether legislation should be adjusted, repealed, or otherwise changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: REFIT and simplification obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: All evaluations and impact assessments accompanying proposals for legislative revision have to analyse the potential for simplification and burden reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: REFIT identifies opportunities to simplify laws, streamline procedures and eliminate unnecessary burdens; consider digital solutions. Quantify compliance costs where feasible and proportionate and present adjustment/administrative costs transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: ‘One in, one out’ approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission offsets new burdens imposed on individuals or businesses by its proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope applies to initiatives accompanied by impact assessments with significant cost implications. Impact assessments should set out estimates of adjustment and administrative costs; administrative burdens are subject to offsetting via the dedicated online administrative burden calculator and reporting. Flexibility includes within-period adjustments, trading across policy areas and exemptions in exceptional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control via the Regulatory Scrutiny Board (RSB)
rubrics_metrics.description: RSB assesses all impact assessments, fitness checks and some selected evaluations and issues opinions to ensure quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For impact assessments RSB opinions are: positive; positive with reservations; negative. Positive needed before interservice consultation for initiatives supported by impact assessments. For evaluations/fitness checks opinions are positive or negative. Where negative, DGs must submit amended reports; where positive with reservations, revisions are required to reflect RSB recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political validation and forward planning requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Political validation at the appropriate level is required before substantive work on an initiative can start and before stakeholder consultations are launched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation requires a valid entry in Decide. No public consultation or interservice work should be launched before political validation. Exceptions can be requested at validation or later via the 'better regulation' unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call for evidence and 'Have Your Say' portal usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The consultation system is based on the 'call for evidence' as the entry point for public consultation and feedback, published on the 'Have Your Say' portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'call for evidence' combines feedback to documents (translated into all EU official languages for impact assessments, evaluations of broad public interest and fitness checks) and, when required, a public consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and exclusions of stakeholder consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder consultation covers public or targeted consultations with stakeholders in preparing policy initiatives or evaluating interventions, but excludes interinstitutional consultations, certain expert group opinions and consultations conducted by EU agencies prior to Commission finalisation of delegated/implementing acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not replace treaty- or legislation-specific consultation frameworks (e.g., social partner consultations) and respects environmental consultation rules (Regulation (EC) No 1367/2006).

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Relations with stakeholders are governed by four general principles: participation; openness and accountability; effectiveness; and coherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation: consult as inclusively as possible. Openness and accountability: make process and its effect on policymaking transparent, including to persons with disabilities. Effectiveness: consult when views can still make a difference and proportionately. Coherence: ensure consistency across services in processes, analysis, review and quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards for consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Five minimum standards apply to all consultations: clarity; targeting; outreach; sufficient time for participation; publication of contributions and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity: consultation documents should be clear and concise and include necessary information; technical questionnaires should include general questions for non-specialists. Targeting: reach all interested parties. Outreach: use adequate awareness-raising and adapt communication channels; publish on 'Have Your Say'. Time: calls for evidence (including public consultations) are published for 12 weeks as a rule. Publish contributions and results on 'Have Your Say' and, if possible, DG websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility for persons with disabilities in consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultations should become progressively accessible to persons with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Commission Strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities; adapt consultation materials and channels accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning and conducting stakeholder consultation (three phases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation work should be planned and conducted in three phases: Phase 1 planning and establishing a consultation strategy; Phase 2 conducting the consultation work; Phase 3 informing policymaking and providing feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 1 includes defining objectives, target groups and methods; Phase 2 includes running consultations and collecting contributions; Phase 3 includes analysis, synopsis report and feeding results into policymaking and providing feedback to respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and concision of consultation documents
rubrics_metrics.description: All consultation documents should be clear and concise and include all necessary information to facilitate responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include non-technical question sets for non-specialists when technical content is unavoidable; provide translation where required; ensure documents explain how contributions will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and translation of key documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'call for evidence' document (for impact assessments, evaluations of broad public interest and fitness checks) is translated into all EU official languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive summaries and translated material should be provided as specified (e.g., executive summary of impact assessment in DGT pages and translated into all EU official languages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact assessment report length and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The main impact assessment report should be limited to 40 pages of text and written with non-expert readers in mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use annexes for technical material. Ensure readers can easily understand the nature of the problem, why EU-level action is appropriate, pros/cons of options, and who would be affected. Prepare a separate executive summary (4-5 DGT pages) to be translated into all EU official languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory contents of an impact assessment report
rubrics_metrics.description: The final impact assessment report must contain at least a description of social, economic and environmental impacts; who will be affected and how; and quantification of costs and benefits where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also include explicit statements if any impacts are not considered significant; impacts on fundamental rights; impacts on SMEs and competitiveness; consideration of 'do no significant harm' and 'digital by default' principles; consistency with European Climate Law; assessment of impacts on relevant SDGs; and a detailed description of the consultation strategy and synopsis report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidiarity and proportionality assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of subsidiarity and proportionality must be carried out and is linked to the impact assessment: final verification of subsidiarity cannot be made until all relevant information is collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis will help fill in the subsidiarity grid to be attached to the legislative proposal; proportionality assessment matches nature/intensity of measures to identified problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory memorandum content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The explanatory memorandum accompanying legislative and some non-legislative proposals should cover legal basis, subsidiarity, proportionality, results of evaluations and fitness checks, results of stakeholder consultations, input from external experts, and a summary of the impact assessment process (or explanation why none was conducted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also include consultation of the RSB, regulatory fitness and simplification, conformity with the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights, main impact categories, conformity with 'do no significant harm' and 'digital by default', contribution to relevant SDGs, and monitoring/evaluation/reporting arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation objectives and questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluations should gather evidence to assess how a specific intervention has performed, taking account of earlier expectations and whether there were unintended or unexpected effects not anticipated in the impact assessment or adopted act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should conclude whether the intervention remains fit for purpose, should be adjusted for greater effectiveness, relevance and coherence or should be repealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring system design principles
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-designed monitoring system should be governed by the following principles: comprehensiveness, proportionality, minimal overlap, timeliness and accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring should cover all objectives, reflect costs of collecting information, avoid duplication, ensure evidence is ready by planned evaluation times, and make evidence available to the public with confidentiality arrangements and data protection as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key monitoring questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring arrangements must answer: what evidence should be collected; when and how should it be collected; who will collect it and from whom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear links between objectives and indicators, consider timing and data quality, identify responsible parties for gathering/providing data and account for cumulative burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation strategy necessity and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Sectoral DGs must decide where an implementation strategy is needed by assessing potential difficulties affecting implementation and application by Member States, national courts or other authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation strategies should be prepared for all major directives and regulations but are normally not required for instruments already including tracking provisions, with limited/technical scope, imposing very few obligations, or merely amending few obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation strategy contents
rubrics_metrics.description: An implementation strategy should include all major steps the Commission should take when monitoring compliance of national laws with EU legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should identify types of support Commission services will provide to assist Member States in transposition/implementation and set out arrangements for monitoring implementation including timeline for compliance assessments, possible enforcement action and implementation reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding unjustified 'gold-plating'
rubrics_metrics.description: When transposing directives, Member States should refrain from unjustified gold-plating (adopting measures beyond directive requirements) and ensure a level playing field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member States must provide the Commission with precise accounts of how national provisions transpose directives and may indicate which measures go beyond requirements. Commission will report annually on monitoring application and instances of gold-plating; encourage posting national transposition texts on Eur-Lex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transposition (completeness) and conformity checks process
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring implementation uses a two-stage verification: first a transposition (completeness) check and, once finalised and any infringement procedures closed, a conformity check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Member State has failed to transpose, consider launching infringement under Article 258 TFEU (or in legislative cases, Article 258 in conjunction with Article 260(3)). Explanatory documents explaining how national instruments transpose directive provisions are essential; failure to submit satisfactory documents may prompt infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and reporting of cost estimates in impact assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact assessments should set out and present estimates of adjustment and administrative costs where feasible and proportionate, and justify estimates when a full impact assessment could not be produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to produce an impact assessment where one should have been prepared, present justified estimates of costs and benefits in analytical reports alongside the proposal or within 3 months, explaining how calculations were made. Use Tool #59 (Cost estimates and 'one in, one out').

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of guidelines in proportionate manner and requests for exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines and toolbox should be applied proportionately using common sense; not every step may be possible or appropriate in certain cases (e.g., political imperatives, emergencies, confidentiality/security).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions can be requested at political validation via Decide or, later, sent to the 'better regulation' unit (functional mailbox provided). The approach retained should be communicated externally with justification (typically through the 'call for evidence').

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward planning activities and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound policymaking starts with good planning focusing on political priorities and organisation of supporting processes: evaluation of existing policies, assessment of problems and alternatives, active engagement with stakeholders and preparation of initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for reflection and to meet procedural requirements including RSB scrutiny, political validation to launch interservice consultation, the interservice consultation itself and translation; coordinate lead service, Secretariat-General, 'better regulation' support units and interservice group members to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of the chosen approach externally
rubrics_metrics.description: The approach retained for application of 'better regulation' instruments should be communicated externally together with a justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically done through the 'call for evidence' so stakeholders understand methodology and scope of consultation/assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to make monitoring evidence publicly available (with caveats)
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle all monitoring evidence should be made available to the public, with clear confidentiality arrangements and data protection rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about data specificities and limitations; ensure accessibility while safeguarding confidentiality and personal data concerns.
